- Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept the proposed controller/processor joinder language in section 2.3?

Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + SCCs mapping for review

Hi Marta —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Quick read-through notes and next steps from Redwood legal/procurement side:

1) Joinder language (section 2.3) — we can accept a controller/processor joinder in principle but need to harmonize the indemnity and liability waterfall. Laura will take lead on specific redline suggestions.

2) Transfer-addendum — Ben, our privacy lead on export controls, recommends a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) as a companion exhibit that enumerates SCC variants and region fallbacks. That keeps the MSA clean.

3) Timeline — hitting 2027-03-10 for signature is tight but workable if we prioritize. Internal ask: can Symmetry confirm whether data residency is strictly EU-only for the product scope (that affects the TIA content)?

I’ll circulate an internal consolidated redline by EOD Tue (2027-03-02) and aim to return a single file for your review by Wed morning.

Action owners (tentative):
- Laura: liability/joinder wording and MSA tie-outs
- Ben: SCCs mapping and TIA draft
- Priya (me): coordinate procurement timeline + DocuSign prep

Thanks — we’ll be in touch shortly.

Regards,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Legal Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + SCCs mapping for review

Priya / Laura —

Quick technical/legal notes for the TIA and SCCs mapping I’ll include in the draft:

- We should flag runtime cache exports (token logs) as a processing category; call it out under Subprocessor table so Symmetry can mark any objections.
- Suggest adding fallback model variants that are explicitly scoped to non-EU hosting in the event of export restrictions — short clause in the TIA, not in the main DPA.
- For SCCs: prefer the standardized modern clauses (2021) with an exhibit that maps which clause set applies per hosting region.

I attached a short reference (sccs-reference-2027.pdf) with the mapping I used — will add margins showing where Symmetry proposed different treatment.

Ben
Principal, Privacy Engineering Ops
Redwood Inference

- Controller/processor joinder: Laura has a recommended substitution that preserves your proposed language but narrows the indemnity waterfall to protect both sides. Please review clause 2.3A in the redline.
- Transfer Addendum (TIA): Ben outlines fallbacks for non-EU hosting and a subprocessor table placeholder where Symmetry should populate any withheld subprocessors (see table row comments).
- Timeline: We can support signature on DocuSign by 2027-03-10 if we get your confirmation on residency scope and any final commercial concessions by end-of-day Thu 2027-03-04.

Action items / owners:
- Symmetry: confirm EU-only residency for the product scope OR list regions where data may be processed (Marta / Tom) — due Thu EOD 2027-03-04
- Redwood legal: finalize joinder and TIA language upon your residency confirmation (Priya / Laura / Ben) — will target Fri 2027-03-05 for final signoff
- Procurement: if you need a negotiated order form change, Tom and our commercial ops (cc’d) should sync separately — suggest a 30-minute call Thu 2027-03-04 10:00–10:30 PT if that works.

Attachments:
- Symmetry_DPA_redline_v2.docx (consolidated redline with comments)
- TIA_draft_20270303.docx
